ICS: Fundamentally inconsistent with Motivational Interviewing. Absence of MI Intentions and skills. Missing most elements of MI, and the conversation being coded has no Indicators representing a patient-centered approach.

Generally inconsistent with Motivational Interviewing. Attempts toward MI are missing the underlying Intentions and skills. May naturally, intentionally, or unintentionally hit elements of MI, yet the conversation coded does not represent a patient-centered approach.

Consistencies and inconsistencies with notable attempts to align with MI Intentions and skills at a ‘do no harm’ level. Naturally, intentionally, or unintentionally hits elements of MI, yet the conversation being coded represents a patient-centered approach.

Competent Motivational Interviewing. Primarily consistent with MI Intentions and skills. Intentionally and purposefully focuses on elements of MI, and the conversation coded represents a patient-centered approach.
Proficient Motivational Interviewing. Adept and consistent with MI Intentions and skills. Deftly orchestrates elements of MI, and the conversation coded embodies a patient-centered approach.
Primary focus is on the practitioner or agency goals/values for the interaction with no interest in perception of patient choice/control.
Cursory or paternalistic focus on patient goals/values and superficial attention to patient choice/control.
Appropriate efforts to focus on patient goals/values with attempts to acknowledge patient choice/control.
Successfully focuses on patient goals/values and self-efficacy while fostering informed choice/control.
Skillfully empowers patient through focus on values/goals and markedly enhances patient sense of choice/control.
Primarily directing, controlling, or mandating the patient goals.
Primarily wandering around, following, or subtly directing patient goals.
Attempts a shared approach to the patient’s goals with instances of wandering, following or directing.
Successfully identifies a shared approach to the patient’s goals.
Skillfully delineates a shared approach to patient’s goals.
Dismisses, ignores, or has little interest in patient perspective, feelings or experiences.
Random, sporadic, or tepid efforts to understand patient perspective.
Appropriate efforts to understand patient perspective with moderate success.
Successfully communicates an understanding of patient perspective.
Skillfully conveys a multifaceted understanding of patient’s perspective.
Exerts the expert role by defining the patient problem and prescribing/developing the goals and/or plan.
Leans toward expert role and consistently misses or unaware of opportunities to collaborate.
Appropriate efforts to collaborate.
Successfully fosters collaboration and power sharing.
Skillfully collaborates and empowers patient as the lead.
Absence of curiosity and exploration of patient perspective.
Minimal curiosity and incomplete efforts to elicit patient perspective.
Appropriate efforts to elicit and explore patient perspective.
Successfully elicits and explores patient perspective.
Skillfully elicits, explores, and expands patient perspective.
The student listened and understood what mattered to me.
The student and I decided together what was important to talk about.
The student asked me about my reasons and confidence for making changes.
The student understood and affirmed my strengths.
The student and I worked together for a plan that suits my goals and preferences.
The student asked permission before offering me information or suggestions.
